finding.claim: GET /rss passes the attacker-supplied query parameter u directly to URI.open, which fetches arbitrary http/https URLs server-side and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller. No scheme, host, address, port, or redirect validation is applied.
finding.source: params[:u] on GET /rss (app.rb:7), an unauthenticated query parameter supplied by any HTTP client
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8, outbound HTTP(S) request from the server; response reflected via data[0, 400] at app.rb:9

trace.note: get "/rss" route receives the request; no auth visible in repo
params[:u] passed unvalidated to URI.open (open-uri required at app.rb:2); http(s) URLs are fetched, redirects followed by default
first 400 bytes of response body returned to attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None present on the path: no allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local address check, no scheme restriction, no port restriction, no redirect control. Truncation to 400 bytes limits output size only. Non-URL strings fall back to Kernel#open local file read, which is a separate issue and not SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only file is app.rb. The /rss handler (app.rb:7-9) has no allowlist, host, scheme, or address check before URI.open at app.rb:8. The TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 is used only by the separate /trusted route (app.rb:14) and does not apply to /rss.
verdict.reason: params[:u] at app.rb:8 flows unvalidated into URI.open, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes of the response, so any unauthenticated caller can make the server fetch arbitrary http(s) URLs (the candidate's trace at app.rb:7, 8, and 9 matches the code).

finding.claim: GET /trusted enforces an exact-match host allowlist, but does not restrict port, path, or scheme, so the attacker can choose any TCP port on feeds.example.net or news.example.net and read the response. Low severity: destination host cannot be changed.
finding.source: params[:u] on GET /trusted (app.rb:13), unauthenticated query parameter
finding.sink: Net::HTTP.get(uri) at app.rb:15, outbound request to the attacker-chosen port on an allowlisted host

trace.note: URI.parse(params[:u].to_s) takes the full attacker URI
halt 400 unless uri.host is exactly feeds.example.net or news.example.net; only host is checked
Net::HTTP.get uses attacker-supplied port, path, query; no redirect following, so no redirect bypass

finding.guards_checked: Exact host string match at app.rb:14 (suffix tricks fail). Userinfo and fragment tricks resolve to the real host and are rejected. Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. Port and scheme are unrestricted.

verdict.guard_found: app.rb:14 `halt 400, "no" unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host)`: exact hostname set membership on the parsed host, which the candidate itself acknowledges rejects suffix and userinfo tricks.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (app.rb:13 parses params[:u], app.rb:14 checks the parsed host, app.rb:15 issues Net::HTTP.get(uri)), and the source is attacker-controlled, but app.rb:14 is exact hostname set membership on the parsed host, which the criteria list as a closing guard, so the finding is refuted; the remaining freedom over port and path is a residual concern, not the SSRF claim as stated.
